A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TraMark study. All pages, including appendices, equations, tables and figures, are readable and support reliable comparison despite reformatting and section moves.

before.justification: Section 5 reports original accuracy and model-leakage verification experiments across four datasets. The supplement reports additional watermark-source, client-sampling and attack experiments.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and adds fine-tuning learning-rate results in Figure 6 and an implemented synthetic-label extension result in Appendix A.10.

M1.justification: Appendix A.10 adds an implemented adaptation using synthetic output labels to accommodate more clients than natural task classes, illustrated by expanding CIFAR-10 outputs from 10 to 20. The core warmup, masked aggregation and watermark injection procedure remains unchanged.

E1.justification: Both retain FMNIST, CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100 and Tiny-ImageNet tasks; MNIST, SVHN and WafflePattern watermarks; and the existing distribution, client-sampling and attack coverage. New experiments vary learning rates and output/client configurations within retained tasks.

E2.justification: FedAvg, WAFFLE and FedTracker remain the main comparison methods. The added experiments use the existing FedAvg comparator. New Table 3 summarizes properties of cited methods without establishing additional empirical baseline evaluations.

E3.justification: Appendix A.9 adds fine-tuning learning rates from 0.01 to 0.1 for 30 reported rounds on CIFAR-100 and Tiny-ImageNet. Appendix A.10 adds testing with an expanded output space. Previously stated Section 5.1 training settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Figure 6 adds sensitivity analysis of watermark removal to fine-tuning learning rate. Appendix A.10 tests extending client capacity through synthetic labels. Existing pruning, fine-tuning-duration, quantization, RNP and watermark-hyperparameter analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both specify three runs with different seeds and averaged results. Both retain the watermark-source T-tests and 0.05 significance threshold, in v1 Table 2 and v2 Table 4. No new uncertainty-estimation practice is specified.

E6.justification: Matched numerical tables and Figures 1–5 retain their results. Figure 6 adds accuracy and verification-rate curves for the learning-rate sweep. Appendix A.10 newly reports full verification and a 0.34% accuracy drop relative to FedAvg for the synthetic-label extension, under an added configuration.

T1.justification: Section 2 removes the explicit attack-model assumptions that clients are unaware of watermarking and do not collude. Definitions 1–4, the optimization problem and mask derivation remain unchanged. Both versions leave theoretical traceability guarantees to future work.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same claims of server-side, traceable black-box watermarking with limited utility loss, including the headline 0.54% average accuracy drop. The added appendix evidence does not redefine these main contributions.

C2.justification: Section 4.3 and Appendix A.10 newly acknowledge the client-capacity limit imposed by unique natural output labels and discuss synthetic labels as a remedy. Section 2 drops explicit attacker restrictions, while Appendix A.11 retains the collusion vulnerability. Computational-overhead and theoretical limitations remain.

D1.justification: V2 newly discloses hardware and operating-system details, the default fine-tuning learning rate, and PyTorch-based mask-selection pseudocode. These are documentation additions. However, Algorithm 2's new TopK selection steps do not clearly implement Section 4.4's unchanged smallest-magnitude watermark-region rule.

R1.justification: Appendix A.2 and Table 3 add an explicit comparison of black-box verification, server-side operation and traceability. V1's citation to Detecting Backdoor Attacks in Federated Learning via Direction Alignment Inspection is removed. Table 3 newly marks RobWe as server-side, contradicting the retained client-side description.

P1.justification: Most prose is retained. Related Work moves from Section 6 to Appendix A.2, the supplement becomes A.1–A.11, citations switch to author-year style, and several explanatory paragraphs and cross-references are added. The main narrative otherwise follows the same structure.

P2.justification: V2 adds notation and method-property tables, Figure 6, and an expanded Algorithm 2. The template changes typography, headings and float placement; Table 1 replaces gray non-IID rows with explicit N labels. Existing Figures 1–5 preserve their plot content.

improvement.justification: V2 adds useful fine-tuning robustness evidence, a tested response to the label-capacity limit, and reproducibility details. However, new Algorithm 2 conflicts with the mask-selection description, and Table 3 contradicts the RobWe discussion. These additions improve empirical support while introducing consistency problems; the PDFs do not resolve the intended mask implementation sufficiently to support a confident net quality judgment.
